answers.explanation: Eight 1s: the first octet is the network, the other three are hosts.
With a /16, the last two octets are host bits, so they're all 255 in the broadcast.
Block size 16; 18 falls in the block that starts at 16.
One before the next block, which starts at 32.
A /20 spans 16 values of the 3rd octet, 16 to 31. Leave out the network (.16.0) and broadcast (.31.255).
That would be the broadcast for a /24. A /20 has 12 host bits, reaching into the 3rd octet: 166.21.31.255.
Skip n = 0 (subnet zero) and n = 255 (the all-ones subnet).
